hints: A valid bracket string has equal numbers of opening and closing brackets and every prefix has at least as many opens as closes.
The total length must be even; choose which positions are opening brackets while preserving the prefix rule.
Use the ballot/Catalan count C(n,n/2)-C(n,n/2-1) modulo the prime.
analogy: Count all balanced-count strings, then subtract those that dip below zero at some prefix.
example: For length 4, valid strings are (()), ()(), so the answer is 2.
algorithm: If n is odd answer 0; otherwise compute C(n,n/2)-C(n,n/2-1) modulo 1,000,000,007 using factorials and inverse factorials.
correctness: The reflection principle pairs every prefix-invalid arrangement with a unique arrangement counted by the subtracted binomial term; the remainder is exactly the valid bracket sequences.
complexity: O(n) preprocessing and O(1) per query; O(n) space.
